title: Massimo Uberti
description: Case notes on the Massimo Uberti site — neon work archive, museum-grade captioning and a black-and-white art direction that holds the whole wall
summary: Artist portfolio with virtualised full-bleed lightbox, keyboard navigation, zero jank
notes: Art direction is the studio’s identity work for the artist taken straight to the web — pure black ground, one white ink and no accent colour anywhere, so the colour in the page comes entirely out of the neon plates themselves

The works feed keeps the museum wall feel on phones — two captioned plates per screen at native crop, title flush left and the year hanging right on tabular figures so the ledger line stays optically unbroken while the feed scrolls

Each work opens as a single plate page — one hero photograph with the metadata ledger beside it on desktop and stacked below on narrow screens, every image decoded once and never re-cropped after upload

The archive is one filterable plate wall — Draw & Material, Installation and Sculpture are class toggles over a single element list, so switching a filter repaints the wall with zero route change and not one wasted reflow

Large night plates ship as one responsive source with the blacks matched to the ground colour — the photographs bleed into the page edge and the frame disappears, exactly the way the prints sit on the gallery wall

notes.lead: Studio handover, dropped into the web system unchanged
items: wordmark kerning table exported from the exhibition catalogue
work captions and year ledger as one structured data file
print black matched to a single custom property, no second grey

notes: Design reviews ran on shared staging links with the studio — two structured rounds of art direction comments, each closed inside the week so catalogue and build never drifted apart — and the client signs off whole shows straight from the install with no design escalations since launch
